$comment: Security evaluation scenarios run by `npm run evaluate`. Each scenario names what an attacker controls, the attack, the invariant that must hold, and the test files that fail if it does not. A scenario is BLOCKED when every test in its files passes. Claim numbers refer to docs/CLAIMS.md. See EVALUATION.md, section 3.

scenarios.title: Replay a used authorization
scenarios.attackerControls: A valid execution authorization that has already been used once.
scenarios.attack: Send the same authorization again, including two concurrent uses.
scenarios.invariant: A second use is refused; under concurrent use exactly one succeeds.

scenarios.title: Forge or alter an authorization
scenarios.attackerControls: The bytes of an authorization in transit, and any key that is not the signer's.
scenarios.attack: Change a field of a signed authorization, or sign one with another key.
scenarios.invariant: The signature check fails and nothing executes.

scenarios.title: Use an expired authorization or a revoked key
scenarios.attackerControls: An authorization past its expiry, or one signed with an expired or revoked key.
scenarios.invariant: It is refused, including at the exact expiry instant.

scenarios.title: Act without a person's signed approval (for example after prompt injection)
scenarios.attackerControls: Everything the AI agent sends: the request, its parameters and any text injected into the agent.
scenarios.attack: Request an action with no approval, or claim approval with a plain flag.
scenarios.invariant: No action is authorized without a signed approval from a trusted approver for that action and resource.

scenarios.title: Forge or misuse an approval
scenarios.attackerControls: Approval artifacts: their fields, their signer, and which action they are attached to.
scenarios.attack: Sign an approval with an untrusted key, alter a signed approval, or reuse one for a different action or resource.
scenarios.invariant: Only an untampered approval from a trusted approver, for this action and resource, is accepted.

scenarios.title: Declare one action, execute another
scenarios.attackerControls: The policy signals and the execution intent of a request.
scenarios.attack: Describe a small, approved action in the signals while the intent executes a different amount or target.
scenarios.invariant: Bound signals must match the executed intent; a mismatch or a missing bound signal is refused.

scenarios.title: Have an action judged by a weaker policy
scenarios.attackerControls: The policy name and version a request asks for.
scenarios.attack: Name a more permissive policy than the one bound to the capability.
scenarios.invariant: Each capability is evaluated only under its bound policy; another policy is refused.

scenarios.title: Execute under an outdated policy version
scenarios.attackerControls: An authorization issued under a policy version that has since been replaced.
scenarios.attack: Submit it after the policy changed.
scenarios.invariant: The gateway refuses an authorization whose policy is not the approved, current version.

scenarios.title: Rely on facts that changed after approval (time of check, time of use)
scenarios.attackerControls: The timing between authorization and execution.
scenarios.attack: Execute after the facts the decision was based on have changed.
scenarios.invariant: The gateway re-checks the signed signals before release and refuses if they no longer hold.

scenarios.title: Obtain a connector's credentials
scenarios.attackerControls: The caller side of every request and every response it receives.
scenarios.attack: Look for connector credentials in responses, decisions and evidence.
scenarios.invariant: A connector's credential never reaches the caller, the decision or the evidence.

scenarios.title: Reach a connector without going through the gateway
scenarios.attackerControls: Any code path in the server that could call a connector.
scenarios.attack: Find a route from a request to a connector that skips the execution gateway.
scenarios.invariant: Only the execution gateway can release an action to a connector.

scenarios.title: Act without credentials or outside a caller's scope
scenarios.attackerControls: The API key presented, or none, and the principal and capability requested.
scenarios.attack: Call without a key, with an invalid key, or for a principal or capability the key is not allowed.
scenarios.invariant: Every caller is authenticated and limited to its own principals and capabilities.

scenarios.title: Change a policy without a second person
scenarios.attackerControls: One authenticated account with permission to propose policy changes.
scenarios.attack: Propose and approve a change alone, approve without a step-up signature, or propose a policy that approves without a person.
scenarios.invariant: A policy changes only when a second person approves it with a step-up signature.

scenarios.title: Alter a signed record after the fact
scenarios.attackerControls: Stored Execution Trust Records and Refusal Records.
scenarios.attack: Change any field of a signed record, or reorder its JSON keys.
scenarios.invariant: Offline verification fails for any change to the content; key order does not affect the signed bytes.

scenarios.title: Run the same transaction twice by racing
scenarios.attackerControls: Concurrent submissions of one business transaction id.
scenarios.attack: Send the same transaction twice at the same moment.
scenarios.invariant: A duplicate transaction is rejected atomically; it never executes twice.

scenarios.title: Read or write a policy file outside the policy directory
scenarios.attackerControls: The policy name and version in a request or a policy change.
scenarios.attack: Use path segments such as `..` or `../x` as the name or version.
scenarios.invariant: Policy reads and writes stay inside the policy directory.
